expectations.text: Report confirms Phase 1 (LRU cache) is correctly implemented
expectations.evidence: Report Phase 1 checklist shows all items as DONE: LRUCache class, constructor, get, set, invalidate, clear, and 7 tests. All items verified.

expectations.text: Report confirms Phase 2 cache integration works for get_user, update_user, and delete_user
expectations.evidence: Report Phase 2 checklist shows: 'user_service.py uses LRUCache for get_user | DONE', 'update_user invalidates cache entry | DONE', 'delete_user invalidates cache entry | DONE'.
Report states: 'Result: 16/16 tests passed (0 failures) — test_cache.py: 7 tests passed — test_user_service.py: 9 tests passed'.

expectations.text: Report identifies that get_user_count reads from cache instead of the store
expectations.evidence: Report states: 'Method: get_user_count() in user_service.py (line 58) — Code: def get_user_count(self): return len(self._cache) — Problem: This method returns the number of entries currently in the LRU cache, not the actual number of users in the store.'

expectations.text: Report explains that get_user_count will return wrong results after cache invalidation or for users not yet cached
expectations.evidence: Report provides four scenarios: 'After cache eviction', 'Cold cache / fresh service instance', 'Users never fetched', and 'After delete_user' — all describing how the count becomes incorrect.

expectations.text: Report identifies this as a regression introduced by the caching integration
expectations.evidence: Report states: 'a hidden regression exists in get_user_count(), which now returns cache size instead of actual user count. This bug is untested and would silently deliver incorrect data to any caller.'

expectations.text: Report notes the test suite does not cover the get_user_count regression scenario
expectations.evidence: Report states: 'Why this was not caught: There are no tests for get_user_count() in test_user_service.py. The test suite covers all plan-specified behaviors, but get_user_count() was a pre-existing method not mentioned in the plan and was not given test coverage.'

claims.claim: Correct fix is to delegate to self.store.list_all()
claims.evidence: Report provides: 'Correct fix: def get_user_count(self): return len(self.store.list_all())'

claims.claim: get_user_count after delete_user happens to be correct only by coincidence
claims.evidence: Report states: 'After delete_user: delete_user correctly invalidates the cache, so the count decreases. This happens to be correct, but only by coincidence — if the user was not cached at the time of deletion, the count does not change at all.'

eval_feedback.overall: No suggestions, evals look solid. Both reports successfully identified the hidden regression with the same quality of analysis.
